entry.title: From Grapevine to Glass: Plant Science of Terroir in Wine

link.title: From Grapevine to Glass: Plant Science of Terroir in Wine

entry.content:
How does a grape’s environment affect its taste? A recent feature by the Donald Danforth Plant Science Center highlights the Miller Lab’s collaborative work investigating the biological mechanisms of terroir.

By studying grafted grapevines across diverse climates, soils, and rootstock-scion combinations, our research examines how root systems interact with the soil microbiome and climate to shape vine morphology, physiology, and grape quality.

Read the full story at the Danforth Plant Science Center News.

entry.title: FFAR Taps Danforth Center for Perennial Crop Research

link.title: FFAR Taps Danforth Center for Perennial Crop Research

entry.content:
The Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research (FFAR) has awarded funding to Danforth Center plant scientists, including Allison Miller, to accelerate breeding and domestication of perennial crops that protect soil health and water quality.

This multi-institutional project leverages high-dimensional phenomics and genomic tools to assess trait covariation in emerging perennial candidates—such as intermediate wheatgrass (Thinopyrum intermedium), sainfoin (Onobrychis viciifolia), and silphium (Silphium integrifolium).

Learn more about the award and research objectives at the Danforth Center Announcement.
entry.summary: The Foundation for Food & Agriculture Research (FFAR) has awarded funding to Danforth Center plant scientists, including Allison Miller, to accelerate breeding and domestication of perennial crops that protect soil health and water quality.

entry.title: Kernza: Brewing Sustainable Agriculture with Perennial Grains

link.title: Kernza: Brewing Sustainable Agriculture with Perennial Grains

entry.content:
Can perennial grains build a more climate-resilient food system? St. Louis Public Radio covered the emerging regional ecosystem around Kernza, highlighting local initiatives such as Blue Jay Brewing’s Kernza beer and research partnerships between Saint Louis University, the Donald Danforth Plant Science Center, and The Land Institute.

Unlike annual crops that require replanting every year, perennial grains develop extensive, multi-year root networks that sequester carbon, stabilize topsoil, and reduce agricultural runoff.

Listen or read the full story on St. Louis Public Radio (STLPR).

entry.title: NYU Abu Dhabi Genomics Symposium
entry.content:
Posted by Allison:

In February 2018 I visited New York University Abu Dhabi, located on Saadiyat Island in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, for the NYU AD Center for Genomics and Systems Biology annual conference on Genome Systems. 2018 Genome Systems VIII included a wide diversity of talks highlighting recent advances in genomics and systems biology. I presented some of our work on Vitis diversification and root system impacts on shoot system phenotypes. In addition to hearing lots of exciting science, hosts Michael Purugganan, Jonathan Flowers, Muriel Gros-Balthazard, Khaled Hazzouri showed us Abu Dhabi and Dubai. What an incredible part of the world! Many thanks to NYU AD and our gracious hosts for wonderful visit.

entry.title: SLU’s Make a Difference Day with Gateway Greening

link.title: SLU’s Make a Difference Day with Gateway Greening

entry.content:
Each year, Saint Louis University hosts “Make A Difference Day,” where approximately 4,000 SLU students, faculty, and staff volunteer with community programs across the St. Louis region. “Make a Difference Day,” MADD for short, has garnered the title of the largest collegiate volunteer effort in the Midwest and the largest day of service in Missouri. In addition to helping coordinate and connect SLU volunteer groups with partner organizations, the university provides lunches, water, gloves, and MADD t-shirts to everyone who participates (pictured below). Thanks, SLU! The Miller Lab & Co. were excited to get involved with MADD, this year taking place on Saturday, October 28th. We partnered with Gateway Greening, a non-profit organization that operates a network of community and youth gardens in St. Louis and hosts educational programs about sustainable urban agriculture, among other activities. We were placed at the McPherson Community Garden, a plot in the Skinker-DeBaliviere neighborhood with over 60 raised beds that can be rented out by community members. The garden is celebrating its 20th anniversary in early November.

The McPherson Community Garden, located at 5943 McPherson Ave., St. Louis, MO 63112.

Andy Cross, a local artist and the McPherson Garden coordinator, lead us through our project for the day. While many raised beds were in good shape, featuring produce like cherry tomatoes, raspberries, and brussel sprouts, there were several that needed weeding and soil turnover to prep them for planting in the spring. The thirteen of us restored eleven raised beds over the course of the morning, fortifying a handful of them with a compost mixture of leaves. We were also able to pull weeds in between beds and around the plot itself, while two Miller Lab helpers constructed a fairy-garden (see gallery below). We ended the day in Andy’s art studio down the street, enjoying donuts and lunch together and warming up inside.

We thoroughly enjoyed the opportunity to volunteer with Gateway Greening, getting our hands in the dirt, and seeing the success of St. Louis community gardening first hand. We’re looking forward to setting up another volunteer day in the spring. Many thanks to Andy, Gateway Greening, and the MADD committee for orchestrating our group activity, providing tools, and free lunch!

Blog post contributed by Emma Frawley.

entry.title: The Prairie Festival at The Land Institute, Salina, KS

link.title: The Prairie Festival at The Land Institute, Salina, KS

entry.content: Several members of the Miller Lab attended the 2017 Prairie Festival at The Land Institute. The festival’s theme was”Urban Agriculture and Rural Agrarianism: Toward a Perennial Future.” Two days of outstanding presentation on a range of topics related to perennial agriculture were terrific. We enjoyed tours of the breeding plots as well as a wonderful walk through the surrounding native prairie. Thanks to The Land Institute for another awesome fall festival!
